text.p: The following are the main stories from Friday morning's Austrian newspapers:
DER STANDARD

- Foreign Minister Wolfgang Schuessel wants to put pressure on Germany to remove its border control to Austria as soon as possible, saying Austria would otherwise not ratify the Amsterdam treaty. German Chancellor Helmut Kohl, Italy's Prime Minister Romano Prodi and Austrian Chancellor Viktor Klima plan to meet at a summit in July to discuss the problems with the Schengen agreement.

- Wolfgang Ruttenstorfer, state secretary in the finance ministry, says a foreign investment bank should lead the reform of Austria's capital market. He also announced foreign traders would now be able to trade on Vienna's futures and options exchange without needing membership.

- Social researchers say Austria's current pension system is the most unfair in the world and call for a complete reform of the public pension system as soon as possible, especially for civil servants.

- Ahead of a meeting between the public sector's labour union and the government to discuss further austerity measures for civil servants, the judiciary has threatened to go on strike should the planned measures not be withdrawn.
- Insurance holding BARC, consisting of insurers Bundeslaender and Austria Collegialitaet, has started its merging process by joining its internal affairs and executive tasks in the holding.
- Austria's National Bank announced the appointment of three new board members, Wolfgang Duchatczek, Gertrude Tumpel-Gugerell and Erwin Tischler.
- The conservative People's Party refusal of the social plan for the employees of Post & Telekom Austria could be a major set-back for the company's privatisation.
- Raiffeisen Zentralbank is now showing interest in participating in postal savings bank PSK.
- Savings banks' building society S-Bausparkasse calls for improved subsidies as the government has announced its plan to cut funding of building society premiums.
DIE PRESSE

- Insurance holding BARC plans to go public after having improved its efficiency by cutting jobs. The holding has reiterated its interest in participating in postal savings bank PSK and shopping centre SCS.
- Legal experts say the latest draft telecommunications law might still breach European law.
- 46 percent of Austria's tourism companies expects falling numbers of tourists this summer.
- Waagner-Biro, a unit of Auricon, plans to expand further abroad, while plans are being made for a going public in 1998 or at the beginning of 1999.
KURIER
- Pension funds call for tax-deductability as is already the case with life insurances.
WIRTSCHAFTSBLATT
- The government might sell a 25-percent-stake in federal grid company Verbund to Austria's regional energy providers, which already hold 17 percent of the company.
